newsitem.title: UK: Barclays climbs on positive broker comment.
newsitem.headline: Barclays climbs on positive broker comment.

text.p: Shares in retail banking group Barclays Plc rose on Wednesday, squeezed higher amid a shortage in the market and as one broker prepared to publish a bullish note on the stock, traders said.
Shares rose 18p to 946-1/2p by 1245 GMT in a generally weaker market.
Market sources said Credit Lyonnais Laing was about to publish a positive note on the stock which reiterated its "buy" stance.
"We think the stock is undervalued for a number of reasons," a source at Credit Lyonnais said.
"We feel that Barclays continues to generate large amounts of capital which will fund significant dividend increases, further share buybacks and its cost control is very good."
Laing also forecast a sharp rise in the profitability of UK clearing banks over the next few years on the back of a reduction in cheque usage.
In addition, Barclays is likely to benefit as consumer expenditure grows, since the bank is a market leader with Barclaycard, Laing said.
Today's gain carried Barclays to a record high, and came after the stock rose 17-1/2p on Tuesday.
Traders said expectations that Barclays may be about to return capital to shareholders in some form may also be supporting its shares.
"I think people are quite excited about the Reuters special dividend and are thinking that Barclays may do the same," said one marketmaker.
Laing agreed that share buybacks were a possibility.

"We think Barclays strategy will remain to utilise its surplus capital to shareholders' best advantage. They have demonstrated that the way to do that is buying back their own shares and we concur with that," Laing said.
Traders said a shortage of stock in the market was also helping to push it higher.
